sentences.text: Manoj Sharma vs Malvi Mishra on 7 November, 2025

In The Supreme Court Of India
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Criminal Appeal No. /2025
 (@ Slp (Crl.) No. 4136/2025)
 Manoj Sharma ..... 
 Versus
 Malvi Mishra ..... 
 O R D E R
Leave granted.
This matter came before this Court on the issue of the interim maintenance to be paid by the appellant-husband, Manoj Sharma, to the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra.
While so, the parties were referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre to explore the possibility of settlement of their disputes, vide order dated 02.05.2025.
Pursuant to the efforts made by the learned Mediator, the parties did manage to do so and reduced the terms of their compromise to writing, vide Settlement Agreement dated 28.08.2025.
In terms thereof, they have now filed a joint application, viz., I.A. No. 232175/2025, seeking appropriate directions.
residing separately since 13.02.2015.
Despite their short stay together, several cases were filed by them against each other.

In any event, pursuant to the compromise now arrived at, the appellant-husband, Manoj Sharma, agreed to pay a sum of 1,21,00,000/- (Rupees one crore twenty-one lakhs only) to the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra, in full and final settlement of all her claims, including permanent alimony.
A sum of 25,00,000/- (Rupees twenty-five lakhs only) had been deposited by him with the Registry of the High Court of Delhi.

This deposit was made in the year 2016 and, as per the directions of the Delhi High Court, the amount was placed in two Fixed Deposits of 12,50,000/- (Rupees twelve lakhs fifty thousand only) each, whereby along with the interest accrued thereon, the amount grew to 42,29,335/- (Rupees forty two lakhs twenty-nine thousand three hundred thirty five only) till the date of the disbursal, as per the order of this Court.
As per Clause 6A of the Settlement Agreement, this amount was to be withdrawn by the respondent-wife.
Apart from the aforestated amount, the petitioner-husband, Manoj Sharma, had deposited a sum of 15,00,000/- (Rupees fifteen lakhs only) with the Registry of this Court in the month of April, 2025.

Though the said amount was also placed in a fixed deposit account, we are Manoj Sharma vs Malvi Mishra on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84862538/
1 informed that no interest accrued thereon owing to its short life as the principal amount of 15,00,000/- (Rupees fifteen lakhs only) was, thereafter, released in favour of the respondent-wife on 23.09.2025.
The aforestated amounts together, therefore, aggregated to 57,29,335/- (Rupees fifty-seven lakhs twenty nine thousand three hundred thirty-five only).

The balance amount payable from the sum of 1,21,00,000/- (Rupees one crore twenty-one lakhs only), after deducting this amount, was thereafter paid by the appellant-husband in open Court, by way of demand drafts on 16.09.2025.
The same was also recorded in the order dated 16.09.2025 passed by this Court.

This Court further directed the Registry of the High Court of Delhi and the Registry of this Court to release the amounts lying in the deposits, along with the interest accrued thereon, directly to the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra, by transferring the amounts to her bank account.

The same having been done, an issue arose as to the tax deducted at source (TDS) on the interest that was paid by the bank on the amount placed in deposit by the High Court of Delhi.
A report was, therefore, called for from the High Court of Delhi, and the Registrar (Budget, Cash &
Accounts) of the High Court, vide letter dated 06.11.2025 addressed to the Registrar of this Court,
stated that the principal amount of the fixed deposits, viz., 25,00,000/- (Rupees twenty-five lakhs only), aggregated to 42,29,335/- (Rupees forty two lakhs twenty-nine thousand three hundred thirty five only) at the time of closure of the deposit accounts, and tax was deducted at the rate of 20%, amounting to 3,45,867/- (Rupees three lakhs forty-five thousand eight hundred sixty-seven only), and the amount was deducted in the name of the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra, indicating her Permanent Account Number  BPBPM1290M.
This amount was stated to have been deposited with the tax authorities as per rules.

This letter was supported by the letter dated 01.11.2025 addressed by the Chief Manager, UCO Bank,
Delhi High Court Branch, to the Administrative Officer (Judicial), Cash-II Branch, Delhi High Court, New Delhi, wherein he stated that a sum of 38,83,468/- (Rupees thirty-eight lakhs eighty-three thousand four hundred sixty-eight only) was remitted into the bank account of the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra, after deducting the tax amount of 3,45,867/- (Rupees three lakhs forty-five thousand eight hundred sixty-seven only), which was deducted in the name of the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra (PANBPBPM1290M), and the same was deposited with the tax authorities as per rules.
In the light of these communications, it is clear that the full amount has been paid to the respondent-wife, Malvi Mishra, as undertaken by the appellant-husband, Manoj Sharma, in Clause 6A of the Settlement Agreement.
Given due compliance with this condition, the parties are at consensus ad idem that this Court should exercise jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to dissolve their marriage by way of a decree of divorce by mutual consent.

ii. Criminal Complaint No. OMA No.588/2019 under Section 202 of the Cr.P.C. dated 24.01.2020 filed by the appellant-husband with Police Station Khadakpada, Kalyan District Thane Maharashtra;

vi. Criminal Case No. 3919 of 2017 filed by the respondent-wife, pending before the District Courts,
